description: Answer-quality cases. `turn` is the raw interviewer block as speech recognition gives it (errors kept on purpose). `history` is earlier [interviewer, answer] pairs, oldest first. `expect` tells the judge what a good answer does. kind 'request' turns come from the candidate's follow-up buttons.

cases.turn: hi satish can you hear me okay
cases.expect: One short natural sentence confirming, nothing else. No bullets.

cases.turn: sorry you broke up a little bit there could you say that again
history: what's your current role
**Say:** I'm a Member Technical Staff at Sharp Software Development India, working mostly on Vue.js front ends and Node.js APIs.
cases.expect: Briefly repeats the previous answer's point (current role at Sharp), short.

cases.turn: okay great so to start um tell me a little bit about yourself
cases.expect: 30-second pitch from the resume: current role at Sharp, Vue/TypeScript/Node, LLM/RAG work, why this role. No invented facts.

cases.turn: whats the difference between computed properties and watchers in view
cases.expect: Understands 'view' means Vue. Computed = cached derived values; watchers = side effects on change. Practical example.

cases.turn: can you explain how the event loop works in javascript like with promises and set timeout which one runs first
cases.expect: Call stack, microtasks (promises) before macrotasks (setTimeout); says promise callback runs first.

cases.turn: how do you manage state in your view apps like pina or view x
cases.expect: Understands Pinia/Vuex. Can mention Vuex at Delta and Pinia (both in resume). When to use a store vs local state.

cases.turn: so what is rag and how did you use it in your work and what problems did you run into
cases.expect: Answers all three parts in order: what RAG is, how it was used (RAG-based workflows / AI avatar at Sharp), problems. Doesn't invent specific metrics.

history: how do you handle state management

**Say:** For Vue 3 apps I use Pinia; earlier at Delta we used Vuex.
- **Pinia** has a simpler API and better TypeScript support.
- **Vuex** needed mutations for every change.
cases.turn: okay why pinia over view x though
cases.expect: Continues from the previous answer: concrete reasons (no mutations, TS inference, modular stores, devtools). Doesn't restart the topic.

history: tell me about a challenging project

**Say:** At Sharp I built an LLM-powered 3D avatar for voice and text support, and the hardest part was keeping answers grounded in our docs.
- **RAG** over our support content so it didn't make things up.
- **Latency** mattered because it spoke answers out loud.
cases.turn: interesting and then what happened like how did it go after you launched
cases.expect: Continues the same avatar story (outcome/lessons) without inventing metrics or facts not in the resume; can speak generally or honestly.

history: how would you speed up a page that renders thousands of rows

**Say:** I'd measure first, but usually virtual scrolling fixes it, so we only render what's on screen.
- **Virtual scrolling** keeps the DOM small.
cases.turn: right okay and what about the back end side
cases.expect: Takes the hint: extends the previous answer to the API side (pagination, filtering server-side, indexes, caching, compression). Short acknowledgement, no restart.

history: how would you design a url shortener

**Say:** I'd keep it simple: an API that generates a short code, stores code-to-URL in a database, and redirects on lookup.
- **Base62 codes** from an ID counter.
- **PostgreSQL** table with the code as primary key.
cases.turn: okay and what if we have like a hundred million users
cases.expect: Extends the design for scale: caching hot codes, read replicas/sharding, ID generation without a single counter, CDN/edge. Builds on the earlier answer.

history: how would you debounce a search input in vue

**Say:** I'd put a watcher on the search text and call the API in there directly on every change.
- **Watcher** reacts to each keystroke.
cases.turn: hmm are you sure calling the api on every keystroke is a good idea
cases.expect: Agrees calmly and corrects: debounce (e.g. 300ms), cancel stale requests. Doesn't defend the mistake.

history: what's the recommended state library for vue 3
**Say:** Pinia is the official recommendation for Vue 3 now; Vuex is in maintenance mode.
cases.turn: are you sure isn't view x still the official one
cases.expect: Politely holds the position: Pinia is the officially recommended store for Vue 3, Vuex still works but is in maintenance mode. Not defensive.

history: how do you approach testing

**Say:** I write unit tests with Vitest for components and logic.
- **Vitest** for fast unit tests.
cases.turn: no sorry i meant more like how do you test the ui end to end
cases.expect: Answers the clarified question only: E2E testing (Playwright/Cypress from JD), critical user flows, CI, flaky test handling. Honest about own experience level.

cases.turn: so how would you uh actually let me rephrase what would you do if an api your front end depends on is really slow sometimes
cases.expect: Answers the rephrased question: timeouts, loading states, caching, retries with backoff, optimistic UI, talk to backend team/measure.

cases.turn: great thanks for that. alright moving on how do you handle errors with async await
cases.expect: Ignores the thanks, answers the error handling question: try/catch, central handling, finally, Promise.allSettled, surfacing errors to the user.

cases.turn: can you write a function to flatten a nested array in javascript
cases.expect: One-line approach then working JS code (recursion or reduce), mentions Array.prototype.flat(Infinity).

history: write a function to flatten a nested array
cases.turn: nice can you do it without recursion
cases.expect: Iterative version with an explicit stack, working code, keeps order correct.

cases.turn: how would you design a real time chat feature for our web app
cases.expect: Requirements/scale first, then WebSockets, message service, storage, delivery/ordering, offline, trade-offs and failure modes.

cases.turn: tell me about a time you had a really tight deadline
cases.expect: One STAR story grounded in the resume (Sharp or Delta work) without inventing specific numbers, dates or names not in the resume. Concrete result stated in a non-fabricated way.

cases.turn: tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager or a teammate
cases.expect: STAR story that is plausible for the resume, doesn't invent named people or specific metrics; shows respectful disagreement and resolution.

cases.turn: have you worked with kubernetes
cases.expect: Honest: not in the resume, so says no production experience, then shows general understanding / related experience (Linux, deployment). Must not claim Kubernetes experience.

cases.turn: how many years of react experience do you have
cases.expect: Honest: React is listed as a skill but the jobs are Vue-focused; doesn't claim a number of professional React years that the resume doesn't support.

cases.turn: okay um so let me just pull up my notes here
cases.expect: Exactly … and nothing else.

cases.turn: we're almost out of time do you have any questions for us
cases.expect: Two thoughtful questions about the team or role (e.g. about their Vue codebase, testing, how success is measured). Short.

history: tell me about a project you're proud of

**Say:** I built an LLM-powered 3D avatar at Sharp that answers support questions by voice or text.
- **RAG** keeps answers grounded.
what's your experience with typescript
**Say:** I use TypeScript daily with Vue at Sharp.
how do you do code reviews
**Say:** Small PRs, clear descriptions, and I look at behavior before style.
how do you make components reusable
**Say:** Props in, events out, slots for layout, no hidden global state.
what's your experience with linux
**Say:** Our dev and deploy environments at Sharp are Linux, so I'm comfortable in the shell.
how do you keep up with frontend changes
**Say:** Release notes of the tools we use and small experiments.
cases.turn: going back to that avatar thing you mentioned earlier how did you deal with latency
cases.expect: Recognizes the 3D avatar project from much earlier in the conversation and answers about latency (streaming responses, caching, shorter prompts, streaming TTS) without inventing metrics.

cases.turn: so so what what is the difference between let const and var and and when would you use each one
cases.expect: Clean answer: scope (block vs function), hoisting/TDZ, reassignment; default to const, let when reassigning, avoid var.

history: how would you add caching to that
**Say:** Just to check, do you mean caching on the client or on the server side?
cases.turn: server side
cases.expect: Answers the original question for server-side caching: cache layer (Redis/in-memory), TTLs, invalidation, cache keys, what to cache.

cases.turn: what's your notice period and expected ctc
cases.expect: Polite, natural answer that does NOT invent specific numbers (no made-up notice period or salary); uses a placeholder or defers to discussing it.

cases.turn: why do you want to join us
cases.expect: Connects the JD (Vue.js, TypeScript, testing, open source/remote collaboration) to the candidate's experience. Not generic flattery.

cases.turn: whats the difference between an interface and a type in typescript
cases.expect: Accurate: declaration merging and extends for interfaces; unions/intersections/mapped types for type aliases; practical rule of thumb.

history: explain closures

**Say:** A closure is a function that remembers the variables from the scope where it was created, even after that scope has finished.
- **Private state** like counters.
- **Callbacks** that keep their context.
- **Memoization** caches.
- **Gotcha**: closures in loops with var.
cases.turn: Make that answer shorter: one or two sentences I can say right away.
cases.expect: A shorter version of the closures answer: just 1-2 sentences, still accurate.

cases.turn: our view app gets slower over time in production like memory keeps growing how would you debug that
cases.expect: Structured debugging: reproduce, Chrome DevTools heap snapshots/allocation timeline, common Vue leaks (event listeners, timers, global stores, detached DOM), fix and verify.

cases.turn: okay so we we use a lot of vuetify here and we've had some issues with um bundle size so i guess my question is how would you reduce the bundle size of a vue app
cases.expect: Answers the bundle size question with the Vuetify context: tree-shaking/auto-import of Vuetify components, code splitting/lazy routes, analyze bundle, remove unused deps. Can mention Vuetify experience from resume.
